'Hello, Lyova, I completely lost track of you.' The meaning hinges on 'hello' working together with 'lost' in spoken Russian.

'Tell me, where were you for so long?' Gulya raises the pitch on 'was' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Lyova answers right away.

'I had some important business over there.' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'at' and 'me' in a few short words.
Подожди, ты сегодня был в больнице?
'Wait, were you at the hospital today?' Gulya addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'the hospital'.
С чего ты это вдруг взяла?
'What made you think that all of a sudden?' The meaning hinges on 'with' working together with 'picked up' in spoken Russian. Gulya answers right away.
У тебя на ногах синие бахилы!
'You have blue hospital shoe covers on your feet!' Gulya addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'hospital shoe covers'.
Я просто медицинскую книжку себе продлевал.
'I was simply renewing my medical book.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'was renewing' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Прости, пожалуйста, мне пора идти работать.
'Excuse me, please, it is time for me to go work.' In Russian, the idea of 'forgive' flows naturally into 'to work' without extra filler words. Gulya answers right away.
Он совсем не умеет мне врать.
'He does not know how to lie to me at all.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'he' before landing on 'to lie'.
Катя, мы с девочками хотели вечером посидеть.
'Katya, the girls and I wanted to hang out tonight.' The meaning hinges on 'Katya' working together with 'to babysit' in spoken Russian.
Может, пойдёшь сегодня вечером с нами?
'Maybe you will come out with us tonight?' Nastya raises the pitch on 'us' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Gulya answers right away.
